newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly up, cash hogs bounce expected.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly up, cash hogs bounce expected.

text.p: CME hogs ended mostly higher, aided by talk the cash market may be poised to bounce next week after declining sharply for much of this week, floor traders said.
There was also support linked to the prospect of pork sales to Japan, where domestic production has fallen this summer and stocks are well below a year ago.
Dealers noted the prices for cash hogs in the key interior Iowa-south Minnesota market had fallen $3.00 since Tuesday with a top on Friday of $58.50 per cwt.
There was talk, however, that prices would be steady-firm on Monday with hot weather seen slowing hog marketings.
Japan lifted an emergency tariff on pork imports on July 1 while shipments from Taiwan are still banned after an outbreak of the highly contagious foot-and-mouth disease.

"It's not surprising that Japanese importers are starting to buy U.S. pork now, if we look at low domestic stocks, a lack of Taiwanese pork and declining domestic supplies," a pork trader at a major Japanese trade house said.
"I expect Japanese buying is likely to continue at least until August," another pork trader in Tokyo said.
August hogs closed 0.525 cent higher at 82.025 cents a lb with other months up 0.500 cent to down 0.200 cent.
Floor sources said Lind Waldock and Cargill Investor Services were featured buyers of August hogs while selling interest was scattered.
Rand Financial Services were a noted seller of October hogs while Refco, Saul Stone and Rosenthal Collins were featured sellers of December. Locals were the main buyers of December hogs, they added.

Pork belly futures closed mostly lower, weakened partly by profit-taking by locals after Thursday's limit advance. Prices had been higher early in the day but selling by R.J. O'Brien in the July contract had turn the market around.
Refco and locals were the key sellers of August late, floor sources said.
August finished 0.450 cent a lb lower at 83.650 cents a lb, well below the day's high of 85.150 cents.
